title: A Day on Venus
description: A single day on Venus lasts longer than an entire Venus year. Venus rotates extremely slowly.

title: Honey Never Spoils
description: Archaeologists have found jars of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that are still edible after thousands of years.

title: Octopuses Have Three Hearts
description: Two hearts pump blood to the gills, while the third pumps blood to the rest of the body.

title: The Moon is Drifting Away
description: The Moon moves about 3.8 centimeters farther from Earth every year.

title: Greek Alphabet Legacy
description: Many scientific and mathematical symbols, such as π and Δ, come from the Greek alphabet.

title: Bananas Are Berries
description: Botanically speaking, bananas qualify as berries, but strawberries do not.

title: Lightning is Hotter Than the Sun
description: A lightning bolt can reach temperatures around 30,000°C, hotter than the Sun's surface.

title: Ancient Greeks Invented the Alarm Clock
description: Plato reportedly used a water-powered alarm clock to signal the start of lectures.

title: Sharks Are Older Than Trees
description: Sharks have existed for over 400 million years, predating the first trees by millions of years.

title: The Eiffel Tower Grows
description: During hot summer days, the Eiffel Tower can grow by up to 15 centimeters due to thermal expansion.

title: Australia Is Wider Than the Moon
description: Australia measures about 4,000 km across, while the Moon's diameter is roughly 3,474 km.

title: Some Turtles Breathe Through Their Butt
description: Certain freshwater turtle species can absorb oxygen through specialized structures near their tail.

title: The First Computer Bug Was Real
description: In 1947 engineers found an actual moth trapped inside a computer relay and called it a bug.

title: Neutron Stars Are Incredibly Dense
description: A teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh around a billion tons on Earth.

title: Water Can Boil and Freeze at the Same Time
description: At a special pressure called the triple point, water can exist as a solid, liquid and gas simultaneously.
